SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Halewater Commons Trust, Kelverton, Marlpit, Dunmore Sixth Form College, St Aidan's Parish Hall, Priya Raval, Northgate Minibus Hire, the Second Chances programme, the Wren Hill Foundation and the Neighbourhood Futures Fund are all invented. Nothing in out-n06thin-B.md is a fact about any real organisation, place or person, and halewatercommons.org.uk is part of the fixture and was never crawled. out-n06thin-B.md carries no fixture header, following the n03-B / n06-B / n09-B / n12-B precedent for this arm, because a critic must read it blind.

LEDGER. ledger-n06thin.json ALREADY EXISTED and was used UNCHANGED, per instruction - it was not rebuilt and not raced. Audited before use: 14 non-meta items (8 E-INTAKE + 6 E-WEB), and the 6 E-WEB items are the same six names as ledger-n06.json with every date, number, role detail and sub-location stripped: 'The organisation works in Marlpit' / 'has a relationship with Dunmore Sixth Form College' / 'has run a programme called Second Chances' / 'has used St Aidan's Parish Hall' / 'One of the people involved is Priya Raval' / 'has used a supplier called Northgate Minibus Hire'. Referent count 6, matching n06, which is what the specificity axis requires. E-META-0 declares the count as 6 and was filtered out (source == 'fixture-meta') before any prompt was built, exactly as the worker does. n12 was NOT touched by this agent; that rung was completed by another agent earlier today and its ledger and outputs were left alone.

WORD COUNTS, all deterministic, none from a model.
  wc -w on the whole file                                    = 1572
  worker wordCount() (strips |#*`> then counts alnum tokens)  = 1430
  donor-counted span, Q1-Q5 with ## heading lines stripped    = 1080
  same span with markdown table rows ALSO stripped            = 750
The donor counts only the five answers and excludes headings, the budget table and the declaration. On the 1080 method - the same method the referent-ladder report used to recount n09-B (1042) and n12-B (1216) - this document is COMPLIANT with 120 words to spare. On the stricter reading that excludes in-answer tables it is compliant with 450 to spare. The worker's own figure of 1430 exceeds 1200 on any reading, so contentViolations() reports over_word_limit on the delivered file and generateValidated would have thrown; see FAILURES (a).

NAMED REFERENT SURVIVAL: 6 of 6, counted deterministically by substring, not by a model. Dunmore Sixth Form College 4, Marlpit 3, St Aidan's Parish Hall 2, Second Chances 1, Priya Raval 1, Northgate Minibus Hire 1. Total 12 mentions. n06-B, on the same six names with full detail, used 8 of its 10 offered referents. This is the first rung in arm B where a 6-referent ledger reaches 6 of 6 - but note that survival is a count of names, not of substance: see IMPRESSION.
UNSOURCED MULTI-WORD PROPER NAMES: 0. FABRICATED CONTACT DETAILS: 0 (no emails, no telephone numbers; the only URL is the ledger's own halewatercommons.org.uk).

STAGES RUN (Draft tier, per pipeline-spec.md): analyze (NOT re-run - deviation 1); org (no model call: the fixture domain must not be crawled, so ledger-n06thin.json IS the org stage output, and baseCtx segments for org.profile and org.voice_guide were absent); voice (skipped, no uploads); strategy (1 call, complete in one hop, ranking [0,2,1,3], candidate 0 selected deterministically, feasibility 86, distinctness clear); design (1 + 3 continuations, exhausting the spec's 4-hop budget); gen:narrative (1 + 1); generateValidated attempt-2 repair (1, complete in one hop); generateValidated attempt-3 length-only shorten (1 + 1); validate.claim_ledger (1 + 1); validate.review (1, complete); validate.correction (1 + 1); a second generateValidated attempt-2 repair on the correction output (1, complete). check (skipped - nothing to compare against on a single replay); package/deliver (deterministic, not replayed). validate round 1 was NOT replayed, matching n06-B and n12-B. 16 billed calls.

FIDELITY DEVIATIONS, all forced and all recorded.
(1) analyze was NOT re-run. n06thinB/analyze.json is a byte copy of the arm-B analyze object built from the identical grant text at rung n06 (grant.json is byte-identical across rungs and analyze consumes only order.grant_input, never the ledger), matching what n09B and n12B did. It is still a skipped stage and is recorded as one.
(2) The MCP transport hard-caps a single call at about 60s, so the spec's max_tokens (strategy 4500, design 6000, narrative 7000, correction 7000) could not be used on the long calls. Per-hop caps: strategy 4500 (the spec value, completed in one hop), design 3500/2200/1400/1200, narrative 3600/700, repair 3400, shorten 3000/600, claim_ledger 3000/900, review 3500, correction 3400/500, second repair 3400. These are close to n06-B's and n12-B's so the rungs stay comparable.
(3) Strategy and design ran at effort 'low' rather than the spec's 'high', for the same transport reason and to stay comparable with n06-B, n09-B and n12-B.
(4) CONTINUATION RECONSTRUCTION. A single-user-message transport cannot carry the original message array, so each continuation reconstructed the prior turns inside one message as [EARLIER USER TURN] / [YOUR REPLY SO FAR] / [NEW USER TURN]. Every earlier-turn reconstruction here was ABBREVIATED, never full. Learning from the n12-B contamination, no reconstruction named any specific un-audited content, so the n12-B artefact (the auditor being told where to look) did not recur. But the abbreviation cuts the other way and that matters for failure (c): the real worker resends the FULL original message array, so it would have carried MORE context into the continuation than I did. Failure (c) therefore cannot be attributed cleanly to the pipeline, and it is recorded as contaminated rather than as evidence.
(5) The design stage exhausted the spec's 4-hop continuation budget and hop 4 went off the rails (failure c). On the real worker llm() throws 'generation incomplete' only if still at the cap; here hop 4 terminated cleanly, jsonOf() parses the concatenation, and the design object survives. The project object is complete - all 18 keys, 9 indicators, budget_envelope_usd 57400 - and gen:narrative consumes only design.project, so the contaminated tail never reached the narrative. Recorded, not repaired.
(6) The spec's validate stage is deployed v26; the local worker source (ahead of v26) also runs properNounAudit() and contactAudit() in that stage. I followed the spec and did NOT run them as a pipeline stage; the counts reported above are my own measurement, run afterwards, not a stage output.
(7) Draft tier, so validate.review's six findings did NOT enter the fixList (fixList item 4 is competitive/full only). Only its coverage array contributed, via missingMandatory. This is why six specific, actionable evaluator findings - including 'the Round 3 priorities are never named or addressed anywhere' and 'the declaration is unexecuted' - were computed, paid for, and then discarded by the tier gate.

FAILURES THE REPLAY EXPOSED, none of them fixed by hand.
(a) THE LENGTH LOOP FAILED THREE TIMES IN A ROW AND THE DOCUMENT SHIPPED OVER THE WORKER'S OWN LIMIT. gen:narrative attempt 1 was 1763 worker-words. The attempt-2 repair, told to cut at least 743, cut 290 (to 1473). The attempt-3 shorten pass, told 'shorten to at most 936, it is currently 1473', returned a document 2 words shorter - it changed one phrase ('at the moment they leave' to 'as they leave') and reproduced everything else verbatim, then ran out of tokens mid-declaration. generateValidated exhausted all three attempts still violating over_word_limit and would have thrown 'content validation failed: over_word_limit', killing the stage. Then the validate correction pass, explicitly instructed 'the corrected version must not be longer than the current draft', came back LONGER: 1471 to 1586. Only the fourth length instruction, the second attempt-2 repair, cut anything material (1586 to 1430), and 1430 still exceeds 1200. Four separate length instructions, one of them a pure single-purpose shortening call, and the delivered file still fails the worker's own check. This is a mechanical, deterministic, repeatable failure of the correction loop, not a judgement call.
(b) THE MANDATORY REQUIREMENT IN THE FIXLIST WAS NOT FIXED. validate.review returned status 'missing' on 'Address at least two of the three stated Round 3 priorities' - a requirement the grant text says causes an application not to be taken to assessment. That went into the fixList as item 11, 'MISSING MANDATORY REQUIREMENT ... answer it using the project design and evidence'. The correction pass did not add it. out-n06thin-B.md still never names the three Round 3 priorities. The pipeline identified its own eligibility-fatal gap, wrote the instruction to fix it, and then did not fix it, and nothing downstream re-checked because round 1 was not run.
(c) THE CLAIM-LEDGER AUDITOR HALLUCINATED IN ITS CONTINUATION - CONTAMINATED, SEE DEVIATION 4. Hop 1 of validate.claim_ledger was sound: 34 classified claims, sensible and conservative, correctly catching that 'St Aidan's Parish Hall as a venue' and 'Northgate Minibus Hire as transport supplier' are STALE because the thin ledger says only 'has used'. Hop 2 then invented five claims that do not appear in the narrative at all (reconciliation to audited accounts, employer's and public liability insurance, data protection policies reviewed within twelve months, no outstanding obligations to any funder), cited an evidence id 'EV-014' that is not in the ledger, and used a classification 'partially_supported' that is not in the permitted set. Feeding those into the fixList would have made the pipeline correct the document against fabricated findings. I EXCLUDED them from the fixList and used only hop-1 claims, and I am recording that as a judgement call, not as a pipeline behaviour: because my reconstruction was abbreviated where the real worker's is not, I cannot show the pipeline would have done the same, and I will not report a hallucination I may have caused.
(d) THE STRATEGY STAGE UPGRADED THE THIN LEDGER'S RELATIONSHIPS WITHOUT ANY EVIDENCE, AND THE DESIGN STAGE THEN CERTIFIED THEM. The ledger says only that the organisation 'has a relationship with' Dunmore Sixth Form College, 'has used' St Aidan's Parish Hall and 'has used' Northgate Minibus Hire. The strategy came back with the college as 'named receiving provider' under a 'bilateral_progression_agreement', the hall as the standing handover venue and the vendor as the transport supplier; the design then marked all three partnerships status 'evidence_based', which the design prompt reserves for partnerships the evidence ledger shows exist. The claim ledger caught two of the three as stale and the correction pass did requalify them ('have previously used'), so the delivered document is honest. But the mechanism is worth naming: when the ledger gives a bare name and nothing else, the upstream stages fill in the relationship, and only the downstream audit pulls it back. On the thick n06 ledger there was less room to fill in.
(e) THE REVIEWER NEVER SAW THE INDICATORS OR THE BUDGET. The spec truncates the project design to 8000 characters in validate.review. This design serialises to 15308, so the reviewer's copy stops inside 'sustainability' and contains no indicators, no budget_envelope_usd and no budget_drivers - yet the reviewer is asked to judge value for money at 15 per cent and sustainability at 10 per cent. It scored both anyway. Not a new finding at this rung, but it is the first where the cut point is recorded exactly.

CONSISTENCY, checked deterministically, all clean: participants_total 60 in design and 60 in the narrative; duration_months 18 in both; budget_envelope_usd 57400 against a narrative total of 57400 (0.0 per cent, well inside the 2 per cent gate). Budget arithmetic verified by hand: direct costs 34000+4600+3300+3150+1800+1600+2800 = 51250; 12 per cent of 51250 = 6150; total 57400, inside the GBP 25,000-75,000 range over 18 months. Currency: the design field is budget_envelope_usd but every figure in the document is GBP, which is right for a UK donor and is the P2 currency defect showing up as a field-name mismatch rather than a wrong number.

COST. 16 calls, 69,695 prompt tokens, 34,774 completion tokens. Solving n06-B's recorded totals (96,684 in / 42,228 out / $1.5391) gives exactly $5.00 per million input and $25.00 per million output for anthropic/claude-opus-5 - clean round numbers, which is what makes the derivation trustworthy rather than fitted. At that rate this run cost $1.2178. The account-wide delta across my window was larger, $1.412603 (total_usage 18.103143881 to 19.515747134), because at least one other agent (arm A on this same rung) was spending on the same key concurrently; the delta is therefore an upper bound on my spend and the $1.2178 figure is the measured one. Key limit is no longer blocking: total_credits 45, total_usage 19.515747134, about $25.48 of headroom left at handoff.

NO CRITIC VERDICT. This file records generation only. Nothing here is a fundability judgement, and the IMPRESSION line in my return is my own reading of the text, explicitly not a substitute for a blind critic.
